statement: Every continuous section of a hyperbolic curve over a number field admits cuspidally central lifts for every finite reduced puncture divisor. At the fixed base curve these lifts can be chosen compatibly for all divisors. The conclusion and vanishing of all Picard Chern pullbacks hold uniformly after finite extensions and on finite étale neighbourhoods; compatibility between different neighbourhoods is not asserted.

notes: At a local cusp the diagonal torsor extends and is canonically trivial near that cusp, lifting the given tangential cocycle without assuming its rationality. The only inverse limit used for H2 is over Kummer moduli for fixed number fields, where H1 transition maps are surjective. Compatibility over finite divisors uses actual fibre products, not compactness of infinite H1 torsors. The distinct neighbourhood-compatibility problem remains.

statement: Refutation of the proposed assertion that a surjective trace of permutation Tate modules induces surjective H1 over a number field, and hence that arbitrary central-lift choices automatically descend compatibly after splitting cusp residue fields. For Q(i)/Q the trace induces the norm, which misses the Kummer class3 already modulo2.
